etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English quantite, from Old French quantité, from Latin quantitās (“quantity”), from quantus (“how much”).

definitions.definition: A fundamental, generic term used when referring to the measurement (count, amount) of a scalar, vector, number of items or to some other way of denominating the value of a collection or group of items.
(metrology) Property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, where the property has a magnitude that can be expressed as number and a reference.
(mathematics) Indicates that the entire preceding expression is henceforth considered a single object.
